title: US and China hold first trade council talks on tariff cuts before Xi-Trump meeting
dek: Beijing called the video meeting 'candid, in-depth and constructive' but announced no deal. India, outside the US-China truce, faces a rare-earth deadline of its own on 10 January.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
The United States and China held the first meeting of a new bilateral trade council by video on Friday, discussing tariffs, a reciprocal tariff cut on about $30 billion of each other's goods and farm trade, China's Ministry of Commerce said on Saturday. It did not say whether any agreement had been reached.

The two sides had a "candid, in-depth and constructive exchange", the ministry said in a statement carried by the state news agency Xinhua, and would keep using the council to "resolve their respective economic and trade concerns" and "shorten the list of issues". The meeting came days before President Xi Jinping and President Donald Trump are due to meet on Thursday on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen, according to the White House.

## What is on the table

The council was set up under a consensus reached in May. At their eighth round of consultations, in New York and Washington from 20 to 23 September, the two sides agreed to cut tariffs reciprocally on about $30 billion of goods each, with duties on about 90% of the covered products lowered to most-favoured-nation rates, according to Xinhua. Taken together, the package is worth about $60 billion and includes roughly $17 billion of American farm goods of the kind China imported in 2024, according to reports. It has not been finalised.

Beijing has repeatedly said Washington must carry out the tariff cuts before China increases farm purchases. The record so far is thin: an analysis of Chinese customs data found that China's purchases of US farm goods other than soybeans are on track for a seven-year low this year, despite a commitment to buy $17 billion a year through 2028, according to reports. Earlier this month the US Trade Representative's office said China must take "concrete actions to fully implement its past commitments", naming farm purchases, rare earths and other critical minerals.

## Why it matters for India

India is not part of the US-China truce, but it is exposed to what happens to it. On 10 November China extended its suspension of the sweeping rare-earth, battery-material and synthetic-diamond export controls it announced in October 2025, but only to 10 January 2027, in an announcement by the Commerce Ministry and the customs administration that gave no reason. If the controls return, Indian makers of electric vehicles, electronics and wind turbines that rely on Chinese magnets and materials would need Chinese licences, including under a rule covering foreign-made goods with even small amounts of Chinese rare earths.

A US-China deal that cuts tariffs on Chinese goods could also narrow the advantage Indian exporters have gained in the US market as companies moved supply chains out of China. India's exports rose 30% to about $90 billion in October, government data showed this week.

## What happens next

Mr Trump and Mr Xi are due to meet in Shenzhen on Thursday, and a three-way meeting with Russia's Vladimir Putin is also planned during the APEC summit. Any announcement on the $30 billion tariff package, farm purchases or a longer rare-earth pause would be the clearest sign of what the council has achieved.
